look: Rebel's looted-and-worn woodsman's axe: nicked and chipped edge, broken corner, dented poll, rust; battered
prompt: Museum catalogue photo of a single object: a medieval iron axe head WITHOUT any wooden haft, 14th century Estonian peasant woodsman's axe, old and battered, seen from the side showing one flat cheek of the head. Outline: a solid rectangular poll block 4 cm tall at the left, then the head flares into a fan: the cutting edge on the right is a convex line 9 cm long, the head is 15 cm from poll to edge. The cheek is flat with NO holes and NO openings (the haft eye runs top to bottom through the poll and cannot be seen from this side). Heavily worn: the edge is nicked and chipped, one corner of the blade broken off, dented poll, orange-brown rust patches over dark pitted iron, sharpened thin. No beard, no hook, no ornament, not Viking, not fantasy. Lying flat, poll on the left, edge on the right, whole object in frame with margin, plain pure white background, soft even studio light, no cast shadow, no text.
